health_zone_table.basis: SitRep72 Tableau 2 (2026-07-25) transcribed and reconciled against the INSP PDF (13 pages, sha256 7aaebe9ac2af074e4556c408e4efaf59d5082f50ece2bfd0dc079492de696f5f); every province closes to Tableau 1 and to the national headline with no residual.

reconciliation.note: SitRep72 (report date 2026-07-25) is a CLEANLY ADDITIVE cycle on both metrics: 3075 + 125 = 3200 confirmed and 1354 + 51 = 1405 deaths, so the count-reconciliation gate classifies BOTH as reconciled and the increments are safe to difference. Every province's zone rows sum EXACTLY to its Tableau 1 total (Ituri 2848/1184 across 28 zones, Nord-Kivu 306/196 across 11, Haut-Uele 38/20 across 5, Tshopo 5/4 across 3, Sud-Kivu 3/1 across 1) and the five provinces sum exactly to the printed national 3200/1405 with no residual. Day columns roll up by province (115 + 7 + 3 = 125) and the death split closes (32 community + 19 intra-CTE = 51). A one-case harmonization IS declared this cycle (one case in Wamba, Haut-Uele, after database harmonization in the province), but it is ADDITIVE and already inside the notified +125: the four provincial laboratory paragraphs account for 124 positives, and 124 + 1 harmonized = 125. It therefore does NOT restate the series and does not break differenceability - unlike the SR69 harmonization, which did. Rwampara is again the largest single-zone movement (+35 confirmed, the biggest zone increment on the surface) with only 2 deaths in its day column, both intra-CTE.

lab_indicators_24h.note: National aggregate over the four provincial paragraphs in section 3.2: Ituri 224 samples documented in the collection network / 115 positive (87 living, 28 deaths) = 51.3%; Nord-Kivu 135 received and analysed / 7 positive (4 living, 3 deaths) = 5.2%; Haut-Uele 10 received but only 8 analysed / 2 positive (both living) = 25.0%; Tshopo 5 received and analysed, all negative. Collected 374 vs analysed 372 differ because Haut-Uele analysed only 8 of its 10 samples. NATIONAL POSITIVITY ROSE SHARPLY, 25.2% -> 33.3% (124/372), on a SMALLER analysed volume (381 -> 372): this is the third consecutive cycle of rising positivity on flat-to-falling testing, which is the signature of a rising force of infection rather than of expanding ascertainment. Ituri alone moved 36.3% -> 51.3%. The 124 provincial positives plus the single declared Wamba harmonization case reconcile exactly to the 125 notified confirmations.

care_continuity: SitRep72 Tableau 6: 773 in isolation at end of day (307 confirmed / 466 suspected, a split that closes exactly against the census) at 82.1% global bed occupancy (773/941 beds); Ituri 75.3% (602/800), Nord-Kivu 121.3% (171/141) and still the only province over capacity; Haut-Uele and Tshopo both ND.
The bed identity closes exactly: 743 in bed at J-1 plus 151 admissions minus 121 exits equals the 773 end-of-day census.
Exits over 24h (121): 25 deaths, 77 non-cases, 15 recoveries, 2 escapes and 2 transfers to the HGR. Escapes fell 8 -> 2, both in Ituri.

Provider non-payment produced strikes in the Bunia and Rwampara health zones, with a resumption announced only after the Ituri military governor intervened; safe and dignified burials were among the interrupted activities.
Only 175 of 1170 triage units (15%) are functional, against 123 cumulative front-line worker infections and 37 deaths (30.1% lethality), with a new front-line case reported at Nizi.
highlights: Harmonization IS declared but is ADDITIVE and already inside the notified increment: one case in Wamba (Haut-Uele) after provincial database harmonization. 3075 + 125 = 3200 and 1354 + 51 = 1405 both close exactly, so unlike SitRep69 this cycle does NOT restate the series and the increments remain safe to difference.
No new health zone was affected. The cumulative holds at 48 of 140 zones across five provinces, of which 47 remain in active transmission.
Ituri remains the epicentre with 89.0% of cumulative cases (2848), 84.3% of deaths (1184) and 92.0% of the day's confirmations (115 of 125).

Laboratory positivity rose 25.2% -> 33.3% nationally and 36.3% -> 51.3% in Ituri, on analysed volume that FELL 381 -> 372. Rising positivity on falling testing is the signature of a rising force of infection, not of expanding ascertainment.
Community deaths remain the majority of Ituri's mortality: 28 of 42 confirmed deaths (66.7%) were community swab-positive, and 4 of 8 (50.0%) in Nord-Kivu.

Ituri added 91 beds (709 -> 800), the largest single-cycle capacity addition in the recent series, consistent with the Rwampara CTE reaching 100 operational beds. Nord-Kivu added none and stays over capacity at 121.3%.

Sud-Kivu returned to the alert table for the first time in the recent series (8 alerts, 7 investigated, 7 validated living), so all five provinces now report alerts even though Sud-Kivu's contact follow-up is closed and Miti-Murhesa has 60 days without a confirmed case.
Rwampara recorded the largest single-zone increment on the surface (+35 confirmed) with only 2 deaths in its day column, both intra-CTE and none community.

alerts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 3 (at 25/07): 1417 alerts of the day (1335 new + 82 Report-J-1) and for the FIRST time in the recent series ALL FIVE provinces report, Sud-Kivu included (8 alerts, 7 investigated). Province rows sum exactly (588+747+52+22+8 = 1417 reported; 482+707+6+4+7 = 1206 investigated; 168+54+2+2+7 = 233 living; 74+32+1+0+0 = 107 community deaths; 242+86+3+2+7 = 340 suspects, and 233 + 107 = 340). National investigation rate rises 83.5% -> 85.1% on a SMALLER volume (1937 -> 1417 reported), so this cycle's gain is partly a denominator effect and is not comparable to SitRep71's gain, which came on rising volume. ITURI FELL BACK: 74.0% -> 81.9% is a rise in rate but on volume that dropped 866 -> 588, and its raw investigated count fell 641 -> 482. HAUT-UELE IS THE FAILURE POINT: 11.5% (6 of 52), with 41 of those 52 carried over from the previous day - the worst rate on the surface for a second consecutive cycle, and its carried-over backlog now exceeds its new alerts (41 carried vs 11 new). Nord-Kivu holds at 94.7% as printed.

challenges.finding: Reluctance toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams (attack at the Muchanga bridge, activities paralysed at Nyankunde) delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.
challenges.response: Intensify CREC/RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure the teams and increase the number of EDS teams.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of front-line providers, with strikes in the Bunia and Rwampara health zones; a resumption was announced after the intervention of Ituri's military governor. Response activities including safe and dignified burials are interrupted.
challenges.response: Regularise provider payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: CTE/CT capacity is insufficient: 121.3% occupancy in Nord-Kivu (141 beds) and 75.1% in Ituri (602 patients for 800 beds), causing admission delays and raising nosocomial transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Contact-tracing performance is weak: Ituri 75.6%, Nord-Kivu 83.7%, Haut-Uele 64.8% and Tshopo 90.9%, leaving transmission chains uninterrupted.
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays (RECO); reinforce supervision; investigate the drop observed in Ituri.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and pre-positioning at control points delay transfer and isolation.
challenges.response: Pre-position ambulances including at PoE/PoC and deploy a treatment centre per health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient supply of essential medicines (MEG) and medical inputs weakens holistic case management.
challenges.response: Advocacy and urgent procurement of essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited functional triage units (175 of 1170, or 15%) drive a high nosocomial infection risk (123 front-line worker cases, 37 deaths).
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforcement of IPC training.

challenges.finding: Geographic extension to Haut-Uele and Tshopo alongside high mobility raises the risk of urban, riverine and cross-border spread.
challenges.response: Activate the 23 priority PoE/PoC in Haut-Uele and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Proximity laboratories at Butembo and Mambasa are not yet installed, so confirmation delays stay long and transmission goes undetected.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across the pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilisation and advocacy with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential health services (CEHS) is compromised, raising indirect non-Ebola mortality.
challenges.response: Effective implementation of free care and reinforcement of CEHS.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 4 (25 July): 15440 under follow-up, 12010 seen, 77.8% national, still far below the 95% operational threshold. Province rows sum exactly (10901+4307+33+199+0 = 15440; 8245+3606+30+129+0 = 12010). THE DENOMINATOR MOVED AGAIN, in the opposite direction: the source keeps its asterisk (Ituri and Nord-Kivu rates are computed ONLY over health zones that reported), but the non-reporting SET CHANGED COMPOSITION AND GREW from eight zones to ten - now Damas, Fataki, Kilo, Kambala, Logo, Mambasa, Nyankunde, Rimba, Masereka and Mutwanga. Bambu, Gety, Lolwa and Mahagi returned to reporting; Fataki, Kilo, Mambasa, Nyankunde, Kambala and Logo dropped out. Ituri's cohort consequently REBOUNDED 10123 -> 10901 (+778) after last cycle's -1209 contraction, and its rate rose 73.8% -> 75.6%. Because the cohort membership changed in BOTH directions across the two cycles, neither the SR71 fall nor the SR72 recovery can be read as a change in field performance; the rate is measured on a moving denominator and remains UNINTERPRETABLE as a trend. Nord-Kivu's cohort grew 4111 -> 4307 with the rate at 83.7%. Haut-Uele reports for a second cycle and DETERIORATED sharply, 72.1% -> 64.8% on a cohort that shrank 258 -> 199. Tshopo holds 90.9% (30/33). Sud-Kivu remains closed (0/0, NA). 'Mutwanga' again appears in the source's non-reporting list but is not on the 48-zone affected roster; it is preserved as printed and not added.

patient_movement_total.data_gap_note: SitRep72 Tableau 6 end-of-day census 773 at 82.1% occupancy (773/941 beds): Ituri 602 @75.3% (800 beds, 287 confirmed / 315 suspected), Nord-Kivu 171 @121.3% (141 beds, 20 / 151); Haut-Uele AND Tshopo again report ND. The confirmed/suspect split closes exactly (307 + 466 = 773, and each reporting province closes: Ituri 287+315 = 602, Nord-Kivu 20+151 = 171). The bed identity closes exactly (743 J-1 + 151 admissions - 121 exits = 773). Exits over 24h (121 total): 25 deaths, 77 non-cases, 15 recoveries, 2 escapes, 2 HGR transfers. ITURI BED CAPACITY JUMPED 709 -> 800 (+91), the largest single-cycle capacity addition in the recent series, consistent with the logistics pillar reporting the Rwampara CTE at 100 operational beds; that addition, not a fall in patients, is what moves Ituri occupancy 81.2% -> 75.3% on a census that is flat at 576 -> 602. Nord-Kivu remains the only province over capacity and WORSENED 126.9% -> 121.3% only in rate while its bed count stayed frozen at 141 for a third consecutive cycle. National capacity rose 850 -> 941 entirely on the Ituri addition. Escapes FELL 8 -> 2 (both Ituri); escapes are a period flow and are summed across cycles, never carried as a stock.

priorities.priority: Stabilise the reporting denominator before reading any rate. The non-reporting set changed composition and grew from eight zones to ten (Damas, Fataki, Kilo, Kambala, Logo, Mambasa, Nyankunde, Rimba, Masereka, Mutwanga), so Ituri's 10123 -> 10901 rebound and its 73.8% -> 75.6% rise are denominator artefacts, not recovered field performance.

Haut-Uele is the failure point at 11.5% (6 of 52) with 41 alerts carried from the previous day, a carried-over backlog now larger than its new alerts. Restore investigation capacity there before the province's 38 cases across 5 zones expand further.
Nord-Kivu remains the only province over capacity at 121.3% on a bed count frozen at 141 for a third consecutive cycle. Ituri absorbed +91 beds this cycle; Nord-Kivu absorbed none.

Positivity rose 25.2% -> 33.3% on falling analysed volume, with Ituri at 51.3%. Install the Butembo and Mambasa proximity laboratories: confirmation delay is now the binding constraint on both case-finding and isolation.
123 cumulative front-line worker infections with 37 deaths (30.1% lethality) and a new Nizi case this cycle, against only 15% of triage units functional (175 of 1170).

Provider non-payment produced strikes in Bunia and Rwampara, the two largest-caseload zones in the country. Payment regularisation is now an epidemiological control measure, not an administrative one.

preserved_conflicts: SitRep72 national headline is DRC-only (3200 confirmed / 1405 confirmed deaths across five provinces); the country-scope snapshot adds the Uganda component (20/2/11) separately -> 3220 confirmed / 1407 deaths / 582 recovered. Uganda MoH reports no new cases through 2026-07-21 against a cumulative of 20 (last positive 2026-06-21), so the anchor is carried unchanged on a confirmed rather than an asserted basis.

OCCUPANCY DISAGREEMENT, Ituri: Tableau 6 prints 75,3% while challenge 3 in section 8 prints 75,1% for the same 602 patients over 800 beds (true value 75.25%). Both are preserved as printed; the Tableau 6 figure is used as the operational value because it is the table of record.
ROUNDING DISAGREEMENT, Nord-Kivu alert investigation: Tableau 3 prints 94,7% but 707/747 = 94.65%, which rounds to 94.6%. The printed 94,7% is preserved as the source value.

NARRATIVE OMISSION: the section 1 Ituri zone list (Rwampara 35, Bunia 23, Nizi 20, Nia-Nia 11, Lita 8, Mongbwalu 8, Damas 2, Komanda 2, Mambasa 2, Mangala 2, Mahagi 1) sums to 114, one short of the 115 printed in both Tableau 1 and Tableau 2. Adja (+1) appears in Tableau 2's day column but is missing from the narrative list. The tables are treated as authoritative.

STALE CARRIED TEXT: challenge 4 asks to 'investigate the drop observed in Ituri' in contact tracing, but Ituri's printed follow-up rate ROSE this cycle (73.8% -> 75.6%). The instruction appears carried from an earlier SitRep. Preserved as printed and NOT used as evidence of a current decline.

Nord-Kivu patients-in-bed at J-1 is printed as 167, but SitRep71's end-of-day census for Nord-Kivu was 179 (-12 unexplained). Ituri's J-1 576 matches SitRep71's end-of-day 576 exactly. The discrepancy is preserved; the national bed identity nonetheless closes exactly on the printed J-1 total of 743.

Zone name spelling: Tableau 2 prints 'Gethy' while the cover-page zone roster prints 'Gety'. Both refer to the same Ituri health zone; the roster spelling is used as the canonical key and the table spelling is preserved as printed.
'Mutwanga' appears in the Tableau 4 footnote list of non-reporting zones but is not on the 48-zone affected roster. Preserved as printed and NOT added to the roster.

Haut-Uele laboratory: 10 samples received but only 8 analysed. The 2 unanalysed samples are neither positive nor negative and are excluded from the positivity denominator rather than counted as negative.
Lethality by province is printed to one decimal in Tableau 1 and recomputes exactly from the zone rows in every province, so no provincial CFR conflict exists this cycle.
